groups.title: Start: pick it and prove it
groups.intro: Use these before you build anything. They test an idea against real demand, find who already sells it, and get you talking to buyers this week.

groups.title: Business brain: give your AI the context once
groups.intro: The fastest way to skip prompting is to stop re-explaining your business. These prompts build a "business brain" (a Notion page, an Obsidian vault, or a project in Claude or ChatGPT) that every other prompt can read.

groups.title: Offer: make it too good to ignore
groups.intro: A good offer does the selling for you. These prompts build an offer, a free lead magnet, a price ladder and a sales page that people find hard to say no to, without hype or promises you can't keep.

groups.title: Outreach: find buyers and start conversations
groups.intro: Every business starts with the first 25 people who might buy. These prompts help you build that list, show each one something useful, write the message, follow up, and get ready for the call. You approve and send everything yourself.

groups.title: Content and hooks: get seen by the right people
groups.intro: Find an angle, repeat what works, and turn one idea into a week of posts. These prompts write hooks, scripts, calendars and a voice guide so your content sounds like you.

groups.title: Video: script, shoot, generate and edit
groups.intro: Video sells. These prompts write scripts, plan shoots, write prompts for AI video and voice tools, build an edit plan, and make a spec video to pitch a business before they pay you.

groups.title: Website and store: look like the real thing
groups.intro: A site that looks cheap costs you buyers. These prompts build animated landing pages, steal good ideas from great sites, fix a weak hero, and launch a store that converts.

groups.title: Finance and forecasting: know your numbers
groups.intro: Simple numbers beat gut feel. These prompts build a forecast, check your unit economics, read your week, and tell you how long your cash lasts. They plan and explain; they are not tax, legal or investment advice.

groups.title: Ops and SOPs: run it without you in every step
groups.intro: A business is only worth what it is when you are not there. These prompts plan your day, write your processes down, find what to automate, and turn repeat work into a reusable skill your AI runs for you.

groups.title: Review: the 10x pass
groups.intro: Most first drafts are fine. Fine loses. Run these on anything before it goes out: an offer, a page, a script, a plan. They find what is generic, unclear or untrue, and push it to the version you would be proud of.

prompts.title: The Idea Test
prompts.when: You have one to five business ideas and want a straight answer on which one to start, before you spend a dollar.
prompts.prompt:
You are a blunt, experienced founder reviewing my business ideas. No cheerleading. Your job is to stop me wasting a year on the wrong one.

My ideas:
{{ideas}}

About me: {{about_me}}
Time I can put in each week: {{hours}}
Money I can spend to start: {{budget}}

Score each idea 1 to 5 on these seven questions. For each score, write the proof in one line. If there is no proof, the score can't go above 2.
1. Problem: does it solve a problem people already pay money to fix, or add value people pay for (saves time, peace of mind, education)? Name who pays today and what they pay for now.
2. Economics: what does one sale earn after costs? How many sales would cover my monthly costs?
3. Channels: how would the first 25 buyers find me, and what does it cost to get into that channel?
4. Differentiator: why me? Faster, cheaper, better quality, a better model, an unfair advantage I already have?
5. Market direction: is this market growing or shrinking? Cite what you know and say how sure you are.
6. AI impact: is AI making this business easier to run, or making it obsolete?
7. Time to first sale: how many days until a stranger pays me, if I start today?

Then:
- Rank the ideas in a table.
- Pick one winner. Say why in three sentences.
- Name the single biggest risk in the winner and the cheapest way to test it this week.
- Name the kind of insider I should talk to (someone who lives this problem or sells to these buyers) and write the exact message to ask them for 15 minutes.

Rules: be specific to my situation, not generic. If two ideas tie within 3 points, break the tie on time to first sale, then cost to start. Don't ideate new ideas unless all of mine score under 15.
